_note: Engine-only settings. Every threshold, weight, utility bound and tolerance of the missions lives in mission_scoring.json and is NOT repeated here. Each setting has a value and a why; every one is also listed in /ASSUMPTIONS.md with its effect on results.

engine_version.why: Version of the engine code that produced a bundle; written into manifest.json so a bundle can be traced to the code. The package's __version__ is read from here. 2.0.0: dataset descriptors (engine/datasets.json), the real 1-degree tables, column aliases, provenance from the builders' CSV files, three-level comparability, the v2 binary bundle. 1.1.0: review fixes (unrounded final score, rank on published final, comparability exclusions, ocean fills exported as null, polygon country labels).

mission_config.why: The team's new filter system. All gates, soft weights, bad/good bounds and category tables come from this file.

missions.why: All four missions defined in mission_scoring.json, in its order. rover and ice are marked provisional by their authors and are kept exactly as written, with the provisional flag exported (pending team confirmation).

elevation_m.reason: The common gate elevation_m >= 1 is a land mask written for Earth (its why says 'solo tierra firme, descarta oceano, que el modelo fija en -250 m'). Lunar elevation_m is height relative to a datum (LOLA, 1737.4 km sphere), so on the Moon the same gate would remove 11,041 of 16,200 cells for no physical reason (audit A3 section 2). On the real 1-degree table lunar elevation_m is above the 1737.4 km sphere too and 43,502 of 64,800 lunar cells are below 1 m (real_data/README.md), so the gate stays Earth-only there as well.

mask_fraction.reason: Kept on both bodies exactly as written. On the Moon mask_fraction is the constant 1.0, so the gate never removes a lunar cell. On the real Earth table mask_fraction is the land share of the cell (ESA CCI land cover; inland water counts as water), so the gate means 'at least 30 % land'.

gate_body_applicability.why: Which body each COMMON gate applies to. Thresholds are untouched; only applicability is set here. Mission gates always apply to both bodies. Pending team confirmation.

on_invalid_value.why: A value outside its physically valid range is reported in validity.json and flagged on the cell; it is never clipped, replaced or silently fixed. With today's data no value fails.

value.population: all cells of both bodies that pass the mission's hard filters (concatenated, each cell counted once)

similarity_scale.why: Per-variable physical scale for sim = max(0, 1 - |earth - moon| / scale). A pooled robust physical range keeps real Earth-Moon differences visible: per-body z-scores or percentile ranks would score Earth's largest MODELLED thermal amplitude (38.75 K, formula 8 + 22*bare + 0.0022*elev) as a perfect match for the MODELLED lunar values (63-180 K, formula 180*cos(lat)^0.35). Both ranges are formula output, and the lunar one is contradicted by Diviner (about 250-300 K at low and mid latitudes, R2 section 3; 95-390 K at the equator and about 220 K at polar rims, R3 F10/F12). The population is all passing cells of both bodies concatenated, so the body with more passing cells sets most of the scale (thermal: 16,200 lunar against 2,613 Earth cells); this is pending team confirmation. The rover 'tolerances' in mission_scoring.json are not used as scales because they are defined for 300 m baselines and the *_300m_* columns are copies of 2-degree-cell values.

similarity_zero_scale.why: If a pooled range is zero (every passing cell has the same value), sim is 1 when the two values are equal and 0 otherwise, instead of dividing by zero.

mix_factor.why: alpha in mission_scoring.combine_with_similarity: final = alpha * similarity_pct + (1 - alpha) * suitability. 0.5 is that function's own default (mission_scoring.py line 207). Adopting the library default is still a decision on an open question (how much lunar likeness against mission fitness), so it is pending team confirmation; ASSUMPTIONS.md section 3 gives the effect of 0.3 and 0.7 on each mission's top 10.

pairing_chunk_rows.why: Number of Earth cells compared with all candidate lunar cells per vectorised block. Performance and memory only; it does not change results (the twin is an argmax per Earth row). 128 rows x 64,800 lunar cells x 8 bytes = 66 MB per temporary array on the 1-degree grid; 512 needed 265 MB per array.

value.body_rule: weighted mean of level_scores over the mission's weighted variables that have data, using the mission's soft weights
value.pair_rule: min(Earth score, Moon score) * coverage, where coverage = share of the mission's soft weight with data on both cells

confidence.why: Confidence must say how much the numbers behind a ranking can be trusted. A MEASURED value counts fully, a DERIVED one (a stated formula on a measured value) a little less, an UNDOCUMENTED cached array less, and a MODELLED formula least. The weaker body limits the pair. The criteria act at rover-to-site scale, so a cell larger than high_max_cell_km (every 2-degree cell: about 222 km on Earth, about 61 km on the Moon; every 1-degree cell: about 111 km and 30 km) can never be 'high'. A variable counts on a body only where that body's cell has a value; coverage is the share of the soft weight with data on both the Earth cell and its twin.

explain_top_n.why: Number of top-ranked Earth cells per mission written with a full per-variable explanation in explain.json; enough for a top-N panel and small on disk.

top_failure_reasons_n.why: Number of commonest failure reasons per mission and body listed in missions.json.

body_radius_km.why: Mean radii used for the true cell size (2*pi*R/180 per 2 degrees) and for great-circle distances. 1737.4 km is the sphere of the LOLA DEM and of the IAU gazetteer .prj; 6371.0 km is the IUGG mean Earth radius.

lunar_gazetteer_csv.why: Offline extract of the USGS/IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (MOON_nomenclature_center_pts, 9,087 features, longitudes 0-360 positive east) made by 'python -m engine gazetteer'. Source file and hash are in engine/data/iau_source.json.

lunar_feature_exclude_types.why: Satellite features are lettered craters named after a parent (e.g. 'Tycho K'); 7,064 of 9,087 entries. Excluding them labels a cell with a primary named feature, which is what a map reader recognises (audit A4 used the same rule for 'nearest primary').

antarctic_label_lat_max.why: reverse_geocoder returns the nearest populated GeoNames place, and there are none in Antarctica, so cells there were labelled 'TF Kerguelen' or 'ZA' (audit A3). Land cells whose centre is at or south of 60 S (the Antarctic Treaty area) are labelled Antarctica (AQ) instead, with no first-level region.

export_decimals.why: Rounding of floats in the bundle. Utilities and per-variable similarities are published with 6 decimals and the engine computes suitability, similarity and the final score from exactly these published values, so the browser reproduces them with the DATA_CONTRACT formulas to about 1e-4 points. Scores are published with 2 decimals and the rank is computed on the published final score (ties by id), so the stored rank follows the contract rule on stored values. Other keys keep the input precision of the CSV (variable values), the IAU gazetteer's precision (iau_lat_lon, diameter_km) and the soft weights (weight). The bundle stays under 12 MB.

mission_titles.why: Short English titles for the app. The team's own descriptions in mission_scoring.json are exported verbatim as 'description'.

similarity_comparability.why: A variable that the dataset's registry marks as not the same physical quantity on the two bodies (legacy: provenance.json comparable_across_bodies = false; real tables: datasets.json comparability status 'not_comparable') is left out of the Earth-Moon similarity and of the twin search; it still counts fully in suitability. 'comparable_with_caveat' variables are used and their reason is exported. Comparing bare-ground fraction with a lunar value set by definition, or an Earth air temperature with a lunar surface temperature, would make 'Moon-likeness' measure something else. Pending team confirmation; set false to compare every weighted variable with data on both bodies.

explain_helps_n.why: Number of variables listed in explain.json 'helps_most' (largest final points): enough for a one-line 'why' in the panel.

explain_hurts_n.why: Number of variables listed in explain.json 'hurts_most' (largest lost points above 0).

coordinate_tolerance_deg.why: Largest difference, in degrees, accepted by the schema between a CSV lat/lon and the cell centre computed from row/col. The CSV stores centres with float rounding only; 1e-6 deg is about 0.1 m on Earth.

earth_country_polygons.why: Country of an Earth land cell by point-in-polygon on Natural Earth 1:110m admin-0 countries (public domain). The nearest GeoNames place gave the wrong country for 229 of 5,359 land cells inside a polygon (review). Cells outside every polygon (coasts at 110m resolution, small islands) fall back to the nearest GeoNames place. Source and sha256 in engine/data/ne_source.json.

not_used_by_engine_why.value: tolerances: defined for 300 m baselines while the *_300m_* columns are 2-degree copies. workable_days: not read by mission_scoring.py. domain weights (relieve/material/termico/luz/agua): the team note in mission_scoring.json says they are used only by the web 'Use Weights' button of the similarity; the engine instead weights the similarity with the mission's soft weights, because no mapping from these domains to the new variables exists. This departure is pending team confirmation (ASSUMPTIONS.md section 3).
not_used_by_engine_why.why: Text exported in missions.json 'not_used_by_engine.why' so the app can say why these team settings have no effect.

missing_data_reason.why: A cell whose gated or required variable is empty is eliminated (mission_scoring.json on_missing_gate = 'drop'). The reason code is '<variable>:missing' (as in the v1 bundle and the tests) and the interface label is 'no data: <variable>', so the app can count how many cells each mission loses to missing data (for example Antarctica has no land surface temperature in the real tables).

binary_encoding.why: v2 binary columns: little-endian Float32 (NaN = missing) for cell values and Int32 for everything else, with -2147483648 (INT32_MIN, never a valid value here) as the missing sentinel. Utilities, per-variable similarities, scores and confidence scores are stored as Int32 q with value = q / 10^decimals, using the same decimals as export_decimals, so the browser decodes exactly the published value the engine computed with (a Float32 of 0.123456 is not 0.123456 and would break the exact recompute).

first_view_budget_bytes.why: Size targets of the v2 bundle (2.5 MB = 2,500,000 bytes for manifest, missions, variables, places, Earth base and the default mission; 14 MB = 14,000,000 bytes in total, decimal megabytes so the target holds under either reading), set for loading on a phone. The build reports the sizes and the tests check them; nothing is cut silently to meet them.
